title: Wuthering Heights
descr: Wuthering Heights, Emily Brontë's only novel, was published in 1847 under the pseudonym "Ellis Bell". It was written between October 1845 and June 1846. Wuthering Heights and Anne Brontë's Agnes Grey were accepted by publisher Thomas Newby before the success of their sister Charlotte's novel Jane Eyre. After Emily's death, Charlotte edited the manuscript of Wuthering Heights and arranged for the edited version to be published as a posthumous second edition in 1850.

title: Jane Eyre
descr: Jane Eyre /ɛər/ (originally published as Jane Eyre: An Autobiography) is a novel by English writer Charlotte Brontë, published under the pen name "Currer Bell", on 16 October 1847, by Smith, Elder & Co. of London. The first American edition was published the following year by Harper & Brothers of New York. Primarily a bildungsroman, Jane Eyre follows the experiences of its eponymous heroine, including her growth to adulthood and her love for Mr. Rochester, the brooding master of Thornfield Hall. The novel revolutionised prose fiction in that the focus on Jane's moral and spiritual development is told through an intimate, first-person narrative, where actions and events are coloured by a psychological intensity. The book contains elements of social criticism, with a strong sense of Christian morality at its core and is considered by many to be ahead of its time because of Jane's individualistic character and how the novel approaches the topics of class, sexuality, religion and feminism.

title: The Raven
descr: "The Raven" is a narrative poem by American writer Edgar Allan Poe. First published in January 1845, the poem is often noted for its musicality, stylized language, and supernatural atmosphere. It tells of a talking raven's mysterious visit to a distraught lover, tracing the man's slow fall into madness. The lover, often identified as being a student, is lamenting the loss of his love, Lenore. Sitting on a bust of Pallas, the raven seems to further distress the protagonist with its constant repetition of the word "Nevermore". The poem makes use of folk, mythological, religious, and classical references.

title: Eleonora
descr: "Eleonora" is a short story by Edgar Allan Poe, first published in 1842 in Philadelphia in the literary annual The Gift. It is often regarded as somewhat autobiographical and has a relatively "happy" ending.

title: Catweazle
descr: Catweazle is a British fantasy television series, starring Geoffrey Bayldon in the title role, and created by Richard Carpenter for London Weekend Television. The first series, produced and directed by Quentin Lawrence, was screened in the UK on ITV in 1970. The second series, directed by David Reid and David Lane, was shown in 1971. Each series had thirteen episodes, most but not all written by Carpenter, who also published two books based on the scripts.

title: Dom Casmurro
descr: Dom Casmurro is a novel by Brazilian author Machado de Assis, published in 1899. It is considered one of the masterpieces of Brazilian literature and one of the greatest novels in the Portuguese language. The narrator, Bentinho, recounts his life story and his obsessive love for Capitu, a childhood sweetheart. The novel is famous for its unreliable narrator and the central question of whether Capitu was unfaithful to Bentinho, a debate that has fascinated readers and critics for over a century.

title: Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas
descr: Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas (The Posthumous Memoirs of Brás Cubas), published in 1881, is considered the inaugural work of Brazilian Realism. Narrated from beyond the grave by Brás Cubas, a wealthy and idle Brazilian, the novel is celebrated for its innovative narrative style, dark humor, and philosophical pessimism. Machado de Assis broke with the romantic tradition of Brazilian literature to create a work of remarkable modernity.

title: Quincas Borba
descr: Quincas Borba, published in 1891, is a novel by Machado de Assis that tells the story of Rubião, a simple man from Minas Gerais who inherits a fortune from a philosopher friend named Quincas Borba. The novel explores themes of madness, greed, and moral corruption as Rubião is gradually ruined by the people around him. It is considered one of Machado de Assis's finest works and a cornerstone of Brazilian Realist literature.

title: The Book of Disquiet
descr: The Book of Disquiet (Livro do Desassossego) is a prose work by Portuguese author Fernando Pessoa, published posthumously in 1982. It is presented as the fragmentary diary of Bernardo Soares, one of Pessoa's heteronyms who works as a bookkeeper in Lisbon. The book is a meditation on the nature of identity, dreams, and the monotony of modern life, written in a highly lyrical and introspective style. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest works of Portuguese literature.

title: Mensagem
descr: Mensagem (Message) is the only book of Portuguese poetry published by Fernando Pessoa during his lifetime, released in 1934. It is a collection of mystical and nationalist poems divided into three parts, reflecting on the history and destiny of Portugal. The work draws heavily on the myth of Sebastianism and the idea of a Fifth Empire, and won the Antero de Quental prize. It is considered a masterpiece of Portuguese Modernism.

title: Poems of Fernando Pessoa
descr: Poems of Fernando Pessoa is an English-language anthology collecting verses from Pessoa's three major heteronyms — Alberto Caeiro, Ricardo Reis, and Álvaro de Campos — as well as poems written under his own name. The collection showcases the remarkable range of Pessoa's poetic output, from Caeiro's bucolic paganism to Campos's modernist exuberance. Pessoa's creation of distinct heteronyms with their own biographies, philosophies, and writing styles is considered one of the most extraordinary feats in literary history.
